dedupe_keys.name: loss of 1 500 mw of data centre load in northern virginia after a line fault nerc incident review july 2024

description: This post-event and risk case describes how about sixty data centres in Northern Virginia disconnected from the grid at once on the evening of 10 July 2024. A failed lightning arrester on a 230 kV transmission line in Fairfax County caused six successive faults over 82 seconds, each lasting 42 to 66 milliseconds with voltages dipping to 0.25 to 0.40 per unit; the line's automatic reclosing interacted with data-centre protection schemes that count voltage disturbances in a set period, so the facilities transferred to their backup generators and roughly 1,500 MW of load vanished within two minutes, an amount grid operators had not anticipated. The North American Electric Reliability Corporation published an incident review, Considering Simultaneous Voltage-Sensitive Load Reductions, set up a Large Loads Task Force in August 2024 and issued a Level 2 industry recommendation alert asking utilities to model, monitor and coordinate with large loads; trade press reported a larger similar event in the same area two years later. Coverage: the Dominion Energy and PJM area of Northern Virginia, 10 July 2024. Format and access: free PDF incident review from NERC, with trade-press analyses. Caveats: facility names and exact protection settings are anonymised; frequency and voltage impacts are given at system level. Simulation uses: cascading failure between power grids and data centres, hazard exposure of data-centre ride-through settings, and grid resilience planning for large computing loads. Related records: JLARC's Data Centers in Virginia study describes the same cluster, the NLR and York AI workload datasets give load profiles, and EPRI projections give growth.
